6a(1).fact: Standard PVC softens and degrades under hot water temperatures, restricting its approved indoor supply usage to cold water lines or drainage systems.
6a(1).misconception: Standard white PVC pipe can transport hot pressurized water throughout household plumbing fixtures.
6a(1).pamphlet_summary: Rigid white polyvinyl chloride pipe serves drain, waste, and vent lines as well as cold water service lines where local building codes permit. Assembly requires purple primer to soften the plastic followed by solvent cement to chemically fuse the joints (p. 28).
6a(1).socratic_question: Why do plumbing codes prohibit using standard white PVC pipe for the hot water lines running to your bathroom sink?

6a(2).fact: CPVC requires its own specialized solvent cement because standard PVC cement lacks the chemical formulation needed to fuse chlorinated polymers under high temperatures.
6a(2).misconception: Standard PVC solvent cement creates a strong and durable weld on CPVC water lines.
6a(2).pamphlet_summary: Chlorinated polyvinyl chloride pipe features extra chlorine molecules that allow the material to safely withstand pressurized hot water up to two hundred degrees Fahrenheit. Installers join cream-colored CPVC sections using specialty solvent cement formulated specifically for chlorinated plastic compounds (p. 31).
6a(2).socratic_question: How can you visually distinguish CPVC tubing from standard PVC pipe when browsing the aisles of a plumbing supply store?

6a(3).fact: PEX tubing connects through mechanical methods such as crimp rings, expansion collars, or push-to-connect fittings without any chemical primers or open flames.
6a(3).misconception: PEX tubing connections require chemical solvent cements or soldered joints to create a watertight seal.
6a(3).pamphlet_summary: Flexible cross linked polyethylene tubing resists scale buildup and tolerates freezing conditions better than rigid piping. Plumbers route continuous runs through wall framing and secure connections using metal crimp rings, clamp rings, or push-fit fittings (p. 34).
6a(3).socratic_question: What structural qualities make flexible PEX tubing faster and less prone to leaks during installation compared to rigid copper pipe?

6a(4).fact: Copper tubing is manufactured in distinct wall thicknesses designated by color markings, where Type M has the thinnest walls for interior supply lines and Type K has the thickest walls for underground burial.
6a(4).misconception: All copper pipes share identical wall thicknesses and can be interchanged freely regardless of print color or system pressure.
6a(4).pamphlet_summary: Rigid copper tubing comes in color-coded thickness grades including Type K in green, Type L in blue, and Type M in red. Technicians clean mating surfaces with wire brushes, apply paste flux, and solder the joints using a propane torch and lead-free solder (p. 25).
6a(4).socratic_question: Why must a plumber thoroughly clean copper pipe with abrasive cloth and apply flux before applying heat with a torch?

6a(5).fact: Black steel pipe lacks corrosion protection and rusts rapidly when exposed to water, making it restricted to gas and oil fuel lines rather than potable water service.
6a(5).misconception: Black iron steel pipe is suitable for delivering municipal drinking water inside residential homes.
6a(5).pamphlet_summary: Galvanized steel pipe has a protective zinc coating to resist corrosion in older water supply systems, while uncoated black steel pipe carries natural gas or fuel oil. Both types feature tapered threads that require pipe joint compound or Teflon tape before tightening with pipe wrenches (p. 22).
6a(5).socratic_question: Why do threaded steel pipe joints require Teflon tape or pipe thread sealant rather than just tight mechanical wrenching?

6a(6).fact: The long vertical shaft and pivoting spring-loaded jaws of a basin wrench provide the leverage and reach necessary to grip faucet hardware inaccessible to standard wrenches.
6a(6).misconception: A standard adjustable wrench can reach and loosen faucet mounting nuts located behind deep undermount sink basins.
6a(6).pamphlet_summary: Specialty tools solve access and mechanical challenges unique to fixture maintenance and pipe fabrication. Plumbers rely on basin wrenches to turn mounting nuts in tight spaces behind sink bowls and closet augers to clear toilet obstructions without scratching vitreous china (p. 18).
6a(6).socratic_question: How does the curved rubber sleeve on a closet auger protect bathroom fixtures compared to an ordinary drain snake?
